# Instant

A reading of the monotonic clock.

```rux
pub struct Instant {
    // private fields
}
```

`Copy`. Meaningful only against another reading from the same process: there is no epoch and no calendar here,
which is the point — nothing anybody does to the wall clock changes what [`Since`](/docs/api/time/instant#since) answers.

## Associated functions

<h3 id="now"><code>Now</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Now() -> Instant
```

The clock, read now.
Cannot fail on any supported system: the monotonic clock exists from boot and needs no permission.

**Returns**: the monotonic clock, read now

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Instant.rux#L33)

## Methods

<h3 id="since"><code>Since</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Since(
    self: &Instant,
    earlier: Instant
) -> Duration?
```

The time between `earlier` and this reading, or `None` when `earlier` is not earlier.
Refusing the reversed pair rather than answering with garbage is what makes a mixed-up argument order a
visible bug instead of a wildly large duration.

| Name      | Type      | Description         |
| --------- | --------- | ------------------- |
| `earlier` | `Instant` | the earlier reading |

**Returns**: the time between the two readings, or `None` when `earlier` is not earlier

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Instant.rux#L60)

<h3 id="elapsed"><code>Elapsed</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Elapsed(self: &Instant) -> Duration
```

The time from this reading to now.

**Returns**: the time from this reading to now

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Instant.rux#L71)

## Implements Debug

`Instant` conforms to `Debug`.

<h3 id="write-debug"><code>WriteDebug</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDebug(
    self: &Instant,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the reading as `Instant(nanoseconds: N)`.
The tick count is shown as it is held, in the unit it is held in, named and wrapped so it cannot be mistaken
for a moment on any calendar. There is no `Display` counterpart: a monotonic reading has no text for a
reader, only a difference from another reading, and that difference is a [`Duration`](/docs/api/time/duration).
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for any style or precision — a reading has
one form, and neither a style nor a fraction has anything to select here.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole reading was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Instant.rux#L26)
